title: Bishkek to Chong-Kemin National Park
desc: You leave Bishkek and head into the countryside, stopping first at the Burana Tower, a thousand-year-old minaret left over from a Silk Road city, with old stone carvings scattered around its base. The kids can climb the narrow inner staircase for a view over the valley.

Lunch is with a Dungan family in Iskra Village, who serve homemade lagman, hand-pulled noodles that are a local favourite. From there it's a short drive on to Chong-Kemin National Park, where you settle into a guesthouse and can take an easy stroll through the village before dinner.

title: Canyons & the shore of Ysyk-Kol
desc: The morning starts at the Kok-Moinok canyons, an easy walk among ribbed red and ochre rock that's a good leg-stretch for the whole family. You then drive down to Balykchy for lunch at the western tip of Ysyk-Kol, the great mountain lake that never freezes.

In the afternoon you follow the southern shore east and stop at the Skazka, or Fairy-Tale, canyons, wind-carved formations that really do look like castles and animals if you let your imagination run. You finish the day in Bokonbaev Village, where you stay the night.
meals: breakfast & dinner at guesthouse, lunch at restaurant

title: Eagle hunter & up to Song-Kol
desc: Your day opens with a visit to a local eagle hunter, who shows how these golden eagles are trained and flown, a tradition passed down through generations here. From Bokonbaev you drive on to Kochkor Village for lunch and a short rest.

The road then climbs into the mountains over the Kalmak-Ashuu Pass at 3400 m, with alpine lakes along the way, and drops you at Song-Kol, a high lake ringed by summer pastures. You spend the night in a yurt camp by the water; bring warm layers, as the evenings up here turn cold quickly.
meals: breakfast & lunch at guesthouse, dinner at yurt

title: Song-Kol ride & return to Bishkek
desc: After a night under the open sky, there's the option of an easy horse ride around the lake, passing yurts and grazing herds, gentle enough for first-timers, with a longer mountain loop for anyone keen. Lunch is back at the yurt before you set off.

The drive home crosses the Tuz-Ashuu Pass, with stops at the Kilemche pastures and a few mountain viewpoints along the way. If anyone in the group isn't keen on heights, your guide can take the alternative Kalmak-Ashuu route back to Bishkek.
